**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. History 2 (0560), Paper 2 - Modern World History Since 1870, ORDINARY LEVEL, June 2022. Duration: two and a half hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR questions. TWO questions must be chosen from SECTION A, ONE from SECTION B and ONE other from SECTION C. One of the two questions chosen from SECTION A must be a Starred question (1A\* or 1B\*). Maps should be used to illustrate answers where appropriate. All questions carry equal marks.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.
enonce_intro_markdown: **SECTION A - CAMEROON SINCE 1850.** Question one is compulsory. Answer either 1A\* or 1B\* and one other Question from this section.
incertitudes: Question 4 : dates (Biya Premier ministre le 30 juin 1975, amendement de 1979 faisant du Premier ministre le successeur constitutionnel, démission d'Ahidjo le 4 novembre 1982, serment de Biya le 6 novembre 1982, élection de janvier 1984, tentative de coup d'État du 6 avril 1984, CNU devenu RDPC en 1985) : historiographie courante. Les points suivants sont donnés de mémoire avec moins de certitude et à relire par un historien : démission d'Ahidjo de la présidence du parti en 1983 et reprise par Biya, procès d'Ahidjo « en début 1984 » (condamnation à mort commuée), division de la province du Nord en trois en 1983, suppression du poste de Premier ministre en 1984 (rétabli en 1991), retour du nom « République du Cameroun » en 1984, dissolution puis reconstitution de la Garde républicaine après avril 1984. Le découpage 6/7/7 est supposé : événements 1975-1982, tension avec Ahidjo, mesures après 1984. Aucun bilan chiffré du coup d'État n'est avancé.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Trace the events from 1975 to 1982 that led Paul Biya to become President of the Republic of Cameroon. Why was his relationship with Ahmadou Ahidjo strained by 1984 and what measures did he take to consolidate his rule after 1984?

(6/7/7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** Paul Biya became the second President of Cameroon on 6 November 1982, after the resignation of Ahmadou Ahidjo, the first President. His rise, the quarrel with Ahidjo and his consolidation of power are traced below.

**(a) Events from 1975 to 1982 [6 marks].**
1. *1975: Biya becomes Prime Minister.* A constitutional change in 1975 created the post of Prime Minister, and on 30 June 1975 Paul Biya, who had been Secretary General at the Presidency and a minister, was appointed to it.
2. *1979: Biya becomes the constitutional successor.* In 1979 the constitution was amended so that the Prime Minister would take over as President if the post became vacant. Biya was thus given the first place in line.
3. *1980: Ahidjo is re-elected,* as the sole candidate, for a further term. Biya remained Prime Minister and was seen as the loyal "dauphin".
4. *1982: Ahidjo resigns.* On 4 November 1982 Ahidjo announced his resignation (health reasons were given) and transferred power to the Prime Minister. On 6 November 1982 Paul Biya was sworn in as President of the United Republic of Cameroon, and Ahidjo remained President of the single party, the Cameroon National Union (CNU).

**(b) Why the relationship with Ahidjo was strained by 1984 [7 marks].**
1. *Two centres of power.* Ahidjo kept the leadership of the CNU while Biya was head of state, so state and party had two leaders and orders could contradict each other.
2. *Ahidjo's supporters.* The government, the army and the administration were full of Ahidjo's men (many of them from the North), who kept their loyalty to the former President, while Biya wished to put his own men in key posts.
3. *Biya's reorganisation* of the government, the administration and the army, which Ahidjo's followers saw as an attack on their positions and on the former President's influence.
4. *Ahidjo's reaction.* He went to live in France and criticised Biya's policies from abroad, and he was accused of encouraging opposition.
5. *Mutual accusations of plots.* Biya's government denounced a plot against the President in 1983. After a bitter exchange Ahidjo resigned from the party leadership in the same year, and Biya took over the CNU.
6. *Trial of Ahidjo.* In early 1984 Ahidjo was tried in his absence and condemned to death (the sentence was commuted to life imprisonment), which sealed the break.
7. *Personal and regional rivalry.* The quarrel between the Northern group of Ahidjo and the Southern group of Biya sharpened the conflict.

**(c) Measures to consolidate his rule after 1984 [7 marks].**
1. *Election.* Biya, the sole candidate, was elected in January 1984 for the first time by the people and sworn in again.
2. *Putting down the coup attempt of April 1984.* Officers of the Republican Guard, loyal to Ahidjo, tried to overthrow him on 6 April 1984; the revolt was defeated after heavy fighting, many were arrested, tried and punished, and Biya used this to remove Ahidjo's supporters from the army and security forces.
3. *Reorganisation of the army and security,* with the guard dissolved and rebuilt under trusted officers, which made the forces loyal to him.
4. *Administrative and political changes.* The province of the North was split into three provinces (Adamawa, North and Far North) in 1983, and the post of Prime Minister was abolished in 1984 (it came back in 1991), which concentrated authority in the President. The name of the state was changed from the United Republic of Cameroon back to the Republic of Cameroon (1984).
5. *The party.* In 1985 the CNU was renamed the Cameroon People's Democratic Movement (CPDM) at the Bamenda congress, a new party under Biya's leadership.
6. *The "New Deal" and its slogans.* The "New Deal" policy of "rigour and moralisation" (fight against corruption and waste) and the ideas of "communal liberalism" gave his rule its own programme.
7. *Control of the media and opposition,* with a single party until 1990.

**Conclusion.** Biya moved from Prime Minister (1975) to President (1982) by constitutional succession. The quarrel with Ahidjo, and the coup attempt, led him to remove his predecessor's supporters and to build a strong presidency and party of his own.
